scenes.title: Two weeks of work, ready to reuse
sentences: Software Foundation is intended to turn roughly two weeks of repeated project development into a few hours, potentially as little as one hour.
Developers and AI agents can concentrate on important project-specific work, with GUI, processing, test, build, and delivery connections already established.
lines: ~2 weeks → a few hours → potentially 1 hour
Developers + AI agents: focus on the important work

scenes.title: One application across GUI backends and the TUI
scenes.eyebrow: SHARED GUI ABSTRACTION / SEVEN APPLICATION HOSTS
sentences: One shared application and layout runs through seven GUI and terminal hosts. These are actual screenshots of the same example.
An insulating GUI abstraction keeps application state, behavior, and layout separate from toolkit details. Backend adapters handle rendering, input, and platform services through a common contract.
The hosted browser and WebAssembly versions share their visual renderer, while using different execution paths.
That same boundary reaches the terminal T U I. Application features can carry across supported backends without a separate implementation for each interface.

scenes.title: An optional visual frontend for ordinary code
sentences: The optional editor gives ordinary C, C plus plus, and Rust an event-driven visual frontend. Place widgets, connect events, and open their source.
Ask an AI agent to follow the editor’s project and binding interfaces when you want compatible visual editing.
You can also ignore the editor entirely and use ordinary source tools. Your algorithms remain ordinary functions.
callouts: Ask AI agents to follow its interfaces
Or work entirely in ordinary source

scenes.title: Continuous processing becomes visible
sentences: Visual flows connect multiple inputs and outputs, with typed ports, independent rates, and bounded queues.
The examples include signal processing and a stateful Rust filter.
The same structure can connect computer-vision or other processing algorithms while making their data paths visible.
callouts: Trace the path of the data
Open the function behind a block

scenes.title: Keep developing when services are unavailable
sentences: Retained SDKs, dependencies, source records, and regression tests address recurring development needs.
If frontier AI providers are unavailable, developers can keep working locally with the example, optional editor, documentation, and prepared toolchains.
The graphical HTML explorer and matching PDFs help people find the code to change.
scenes.eyebrow: CONTINUED LOCAL DEVELOPMENT / PREPARED TOOLS AND DOCUMENTATION
lines: Optional editor for forms, events and flows
Keep working during frontier LLM service downtime

scenes.title: GitHub Latest becomes a distro package repository
sentences: One distinctive connection is distribution. CI formats the project’s GitHub Latest release with native packages and signed package-manager indexes.
A P T and pacman connect directly to that Latest release. The user’s operating system discovers updates and fetches the CI-built packages straight from GitHub.
Gentoo follows the same release through its verified sync adapter. There is no independent software-repository server to maintain; the project’s CI takes care of the package publication.
scenes.eyebrow: GITHUB ACTIONS → LATEST RELEASE → OS UPDATES
scenes.note: Release hosting and package distribution use the same CI-published assets.

scenes.title: Carry this work into project after project
sentences: This example reflects work by members of the development team and demonstrates one part of their capabilities.
These tested practices are ready to carry into future projects.
Reusing the foundation can turn weeks of repeated work into hours of focused development, while people and AI agents concentrate on what makes each project valuable.
scenes.eyebrow: ONE EXAMPLE OF THE TEAM’S WORK / REUSABLE ACROSS FUTURE PROJECTS
lines: A few hours, potentially one, through reuse
One example of broader development capabilities
Developers and AI agents focus on the project
